description:
Fetch a public http(s) URL and return its content as markdown (default), plain text, or raw HTML.
- The output starts with a header (final URL after redirects, title, content type, notes), followed by the content.
- HTML becomes readable markdown: scripts, navigation, hidden elements and form controls are removed, the page's <main>/<article> is used when it holds the content, links are absolute, and the page charset is detected.
- Long content is paged: each call returns up to maxChars characters (default 50000, max 200000) and the footer gives the offset for the next call. Calls with offset > 0 reuse the fetched page for 15 minutes.
- Only text content is returned (HTML, markdown, plain text, JSON, XML, ...). PDFs, images, archives and other binary files are rejected, as are responses over 5 MiB; download those with bash or python.
- Local and private network addresses (localhost, LAN, cloud metadata) are blocked; use bash or python for them.
- Pages that need JavaScript, a login, or a bot check (e.g. Cloudflare) cannot be read; a note or the error says so. Use another source instead of retrying the same URL.
- format "text" returns plain text without markdown syntax; "html" returns the raw HTML.

url.description: The http:// or https:// URL to fetch

format.description: Return format: markdown (default), text, or html

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for the whole fetch (1-120, default 30)

maxChars.description: Maximum characters of content to return (default 50000, max 200000)

offset.description: Character offset to start from, for reading the next part of long content (default 0)
